newsitem.title: MEXICO: Nearly 70 pct of Mexicans want ruling party out.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 70 pct of Mexicans want ruling party out.

text.p: Nearly 70 percent of Mexicans prefer the next president not to come from the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has held the top post over the past 67 years, a poll released on Friday said.

The poll by the Centre for Opinion Studies, based at the University of Guadalajara in western Mexico, said 68.1 percent of 3,600 Mexicans polled in Mexico City and 24 of the 31 states want the next president to come from some other party.
The next presidential election is in 2000, but Mexico will hold congressional, gubernatorial and local elections in July.

An even higher percentage, 78.2 percent, said they did not believe President Ernesto Zedillo's assertion that Mexico was emerging from its severe economic crisis, which began with the devaluation of the peso in December 1994.
The poll suggested the conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) could displace the PRI as the leading party in congress after the July elections.

When asked "if the election for federal deputies were held today, which party would you vote for?" 42.6 percent of those polled picked the PAN, 30.7 percent opted for PRI and 13.6 percent chose the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
The poll, conducted Dec. 12-15, has a margin of error of 3.25 percent, the Centre for Opinion Studies said.
